reviews.author: 首尔外围Outcall&Incall
reviews.text: Located next to Seoul Beer in Seongsu-dong, Seoul, this jazz bar is a hidden gem in Seoul. The perfect combination of live jazz music and craft beer, coupled with a top-of-the-line sound system and kawaii piano, creates an impeccable audio-visual experience. The sophisticated atmosphere and interior create a particularly romantic atmosphere on Christmas or snowy days. The chicken is really delicious, so I recommend going up to the second floor for a meal and then coming down to enjoy the performance with a beer. Whether you are a tourist or a gathering with friends, this place will provide you with an unforgettable evening. Seoul Beer’s Best Mark beer is a must-try beer. I'm already planning to visit again for Christmas. Highly recommended to anyone who loves jazz and craft beer. Don’t miss out on Seoul’s hidden gem of nightlife.

reviews.author: 首尔外围Outcall&Incall
reviews.text: This restaurant is located in the heart of the bustling city center and is therefore very accessible. The simple yet sophisticated interior and soft lighting create a comfortable and warm dining atmosphere. The signature dish, braised pork belly, boasts great taste. It has a vivid red-brown color and a rich flavor, but is not greasy and has a texture that melts in your mouth, making it a perfect match with rice and providing a long-lasting taste. The steamed sea bass was fresh and tender, but the seasoning was a bit bland. I think adding more green onions and ginger would eliminate the fishy smell and enhance the flavor. The staff is friendly, attentive and provides prompt service. Food comes out at a decent pace, but it can be a bit crowded during peak hours. The store is clean and hygienic, with appropriate spacing between tables and chairs. However, it can be a bit crowded and noisy on weekend evenings. The prices are reasonable and the portions are generous, making it excellent value for money. Overall, it was a satisfactory experience and perfect for a friends or family gathering. I will definitely visit again and recommend to others. I definitely want to try other signature dishes next time, and I hope they maintain the same high standard as they do now.

reviews.author: pathfinder
reviews.text:
The Taste House 2 exhibition stood out for its delicate curation and the characteristics of the exhibition space. If you attend the docent session on time, you can hear friendly and detailed explanations. Exhibitions are held on the 2nd, 3rd, and 4th floors, and each floor has a different concept. From lighting and interior, furniture and props, objects and paintings, the museum's holdings, various collections, and the parent company's philosophy are well combined. It was also nice to see that it introduced not only the works of great masters such as Picasso and Lee Ufan, but also works by active contemporary artists. It was also fun to be able to imagine various things about my living space while viewing the exhibition. I would like to visit again if there is a next exhibition at Taste House.

reviews.author: un promeneur solitaire
reviews.text:
Taste House: Art in Life, Life in Art
2024. 11. 15 ~ 2025. 05. 18

Swiss-born French architect Le Corbusier (1887-1965) said this. “The home should be the treasure chest of living.”
The name of the exhibition is ‘House of Taste’. It is followed by a colon (:). ‘Art in Life, Life in Art’, art is life and life is art. What do you want to say? D Museum, which planned this exhibition, said of the house, “It is the culmination of the identity and taste of the person who lives there.” It won't be difficult. Taste is the direction in which the desire to do something arises. All you have to do is decorate the house according to the taste of the occupants. Neither too much nor too little. Home is no longer a private living space. It is expanding into a space that expresses the senses and perspectives of residents and, by extension, design. We live in an era where our homes become works of art.
The exhibition consists of three houses covering the 2nd to 4th floors of the D Museum. This is further divided into five spaces. What’s interesting is that the owners of these five spaces were given life by giving them the name ‘Persona.’ As such, the spaces where the tastes of the five personas are condensed are filled with over 300 works by over 70 artists from around the world, ranging from artworks by masters such as Pablo Picasso, Alexander Calder, Kim Whanki, and Park Seo-bo to design furniture by Jean Prouvé and Finn Juhl.
Do I even know my tastes? If I knew, how would I decorate my space? What pictures should I hang on the wall and what furniture should I place close to my eyes? How can I hang a picture I drew and have a chair I made next to it? Just thinking about it makes me happy. It's exciting. It makes me laugh. The moment that imagination becomes reality, at least that room becomes my own ‘house of taste’ and I am as much an artist as anyone else.

Advantages: It is close to Seongsu-dong and Seoul Forest, so it is good to view the exhibition as if taking a walk.

Disadvantage: I wonder why it is necessary to use the cabinet unconditionally. Isn't it too pretentious to say that only one hour is free and you have to pay 1,000 won after the first hour, even though the exhibition must last longer than one hour?

This is an exhibition that combines images of sugar with images of the planet.
There are two buildings, so please refer to the signs carefully.
I understand that you can purchase a parking ticket at a discount by paying about 1,500 won per hour for up to 2 hours.
There are places to take pictures here and there, but there isn't much to see. There are various phrases about sugar, so you can have fun reading them at the beginning of each section. Please refer to the section where ball-shaped balloons are displayed, the section where the tube-shaped wall is made, and the section that depicts various sweet fruits, as they tend to have pretty pictures. I don't know where the fruit comes from, but it seems to have a scent. If you wear bright primary-colored clothes, you can get colorful yet simple photos on the green wall.

reviews.author: Dahlia Kim
reviews.text:
I visited Ttukseom Art Museum for the first time to see the “Shall we go on a trip” exhibition. I visited on a rainy weekend from 12:30 to 1:00, and it only lasted about 10 minutes? I waited at a distance and went in right away. When I came out, I saw that there were a lot of people starting at 2 o'clock and the waiting line was quite long. It looks like you will have to wait at least 30 minutes to 1 hour. Admission is permitted while adjusting the number of visitors inside.
From the moment you enter, it is designed to resemble an airport - boarding gate - in-flight, so you can start the tour feeling like you are actually going on a trip. Admission tickets are made up of passports and airline tickets, and the guides are all dressed as flight attendants, which makes the trip even more enjoyable.
The interior was much more spacious and beautifully designed than I first thought. Various people's paintings, photos, and traces of travel bring back memories of past travels and at the same time raise expectations for future trips that will be taken someday after the current situation is over. It was also a time to think about healthier and fair travel.
As you watch the exhibition, there are stamps in the shape of landmarks in the middle, so you can stamp them one by one in the passport you first received, making you feel like you've really traveled from one country to another. Personally, I really liked the exhibition “Shall we go on a trip?”
I hope that people who are tired of daily life will be revitalized through this exhibition at least once and gain the strength to live their daily lives again.
The photo is only a glimpse of the internal exhibition without spoiling it too much. 😊

reviews.author: Susie Seo
reviews.text:
This is my first time coming to an exhibition. I didn't know I could enjoy it this much. I really had a really happy time! I never knew there was a cultural space like this under the Seoul Forest residential-commercial complex building :) The location was nice and comfortable, and the exhibition felt so good that I stayed with a friend for two and a half hours before going 😊 If you come when there are no people around, you will truly find peace in your heart. I was unfamiliar with Renoir or art itself, but I was able to get a feel for what values, what kind of life he lived, and what style of work he pursued. By interpreting it with a modern sensibility, I was able to get a feel for it. It touched me so much😍👍👍 I highly recommend it. There are a lot of good restaurants nearby, so I recommend a course where you can go see the exhibition and eat when there are no people around!!
I and my friend had a fantastic time indeed. You guys make sure to spend some time here. For us, it took 2.5 hours enjoying every single artwork fully. I guess there was no explanation translated in other languages, but I'm pretty sure you will have fun seeing all the beautiful modern art objects without words. There are a bunch of great eateries around Seongsoo&Seoul Forest area. It would be a perfect day for you guys to visit the exhibition and go for a meal😆 They said 'Renoir would have loved you', and I guarantee once you come see, you will love him and his life too!
